correctness.rationale: For the 16 spanning-tree incidence vectors in the intrinsic 5-dimensional lattice, Edmonds rank inequalities over all 62 nonempty proper edge subsets give the complete facets. An independently written checker used graph-connectivity rank, exact affine ranks and a separate SciPy Qhull support enumeration: both yielded the same 16 facet masks. Intersecting them exhaustively produced 219 nonempty faces with dimensions (16,54,78,54,16,1). For every face, exact gcds of maximal minors of its primitive normal-ray matrix distinguish smooth from nonsimplicial cones; exactly 94 are singular (16 vertices, 48 edges, 30 2-faces) and no simplicial nonunimodular cone occurs. The 30 maximal singular 2-faces are 24 primitive triangles and six primitive parallelograms, with full S4 orbit sizes 12,12,6; each normal cone has four rays, all triples saturated, and primitive relation (+1,+1,-1,-1), which identifies the rank-3 generic transverse singularity with ad-bc=0. Every singular face is contained in a maximal singular 2-face; hence the reduced singular locus has precisely 30 components. The nonsimplicial-orbit set coincides with the singular set, proving reduced equality with the non-Q-factorial locus. The finite analysis is exhaustive only because the rank inequalities cover this fixed matroid and all their facet intersections were enumerated; it is not an extrapolation to larger graphs.
risks: The source supplies a finite classification for this one realizable K4 matroid only; no statement for K_n with n>4, positive characteristic beyond specified char zero, or nonnormal projections.

evidence: K4 is a primary worked example in Feichtner–Sturmfels; its matroid base polytope is the toric orbit closure in Gr(3,6).
Exact independent computation establishes all inclusion-maximal nonsimplicial cones, their toric surface classes and their node transverse germs.
All singular orbits are non-Q-factorial; all simplicial cones are unimodular, a sharp geometric boundary for this specific variety.
value.rationale: The fivefold X_P is a canonical toric compactification of the Grassmannian torus orbit for the first richly structured complete-graph graphic matroid K4. Identifying its exact singular locus as 24 planes and six Segre surfaces, with uniform ordinary-node transverse geometry and a precise non-Q-factoriality obstruction, is a natural complete local-geometric classification. The motivated object/invariant pairing and the local analytic type are not given by a generic toric criterion or the already known f-vector alone. This fixed finite example can be independently useful for birational geometry, toric resolutions and comparison with larger graphic-matroid orbit closures without claiming a generalization or major theorem.
risks: A fixed finite classification may have limited impact outside examples of matroid toric compactifications; no new general K_n theorem or resolution constructed.
